highlights: Ten new topics: loops and nodes, node-voltage and mesh-current analysis, superposition, dependent sources, RL time constants, switching transients, second-order circuits, clampers and voltage doublers, and small signals on a biased diode.
Solutions show their working as typeset math, one step per line, instead of flat text; more problems are converted in the next updates.
The calculator line is upright: fractions stack, powers rise and roots grow as you type; Settings switches back to a flat line.
The calculator gains Matrix and Complex modes, with complex numbers drawn as you type.
The drift problems show the conductor's cut face and its cross-section, and smaller steps lead up to the drift-time problem.
Formula sheets never clip: a long note moves to its own line.
